messages:
Noor: heads-up: ran a bring-up merge of cust-zenobia LoRA onto base-large int4 this morning. quick 'numerics-small' evalpack flagged spacing and missing thousands separators. opening thread to triage.
Carlos: can you drop the eval id + how you ran it?
Noor: eval: https://redwood.internal/evals/ZB-331 (internal)
Noor: repro command:
```bash
./scripts/quick_eval --model=zenobia-lora-merged-int4 --eval=numerics-small --limit=400 --seed=21 --out=/tmp/zen_out.json
```
Mei: paste a couple failing examples (baseline vs merged) so we can inspect detok artifacts
Noor: example 1:
```text
PROMPT: "Total: $" + amount + "\nThanks."
BASELINE (fp32): "Total: $4,500.00
Thanks."
MERGED-INT4: "Total: $4,500 .00
Thanks."
```
Noor: example 2:
```text
PROMPT: "Balance: $" + bal + " as of 2025-02-01"
BASELINE: "Balance: $12,300.00 as of 2025-02-01"
MERGED-INT4: "Balance: $12300.00 as of 2025-02-01"
```
QA-bot: metrics summary (n=400): EM_format fp32=0.993 -> merged-int4=0.68, merged-int8=0.98. TokenSplitRate (numeric punct): fp32=0.0012, int8=0.003, int4=0.127. MAE_amounts fp32=0.018, int8=0.06, int4=1.44.
Carlos: pattern: int8 ~ fp32, int4 diverges. likely two factors: tokenizer id mismap for numeric+punct in LoRA train vs our merge tokenizer, plus int4 quant amplifying small deltas causing token fragmentation. do we have customer's tokenizer bundle?
Noor: yes, they supplied cust_tokenizer_v1.json (with a patch that collapses thousand separators). I mounted it at /mnt/cust/zenobia/tokenizer_v1.json during the test but the initial merge used standard bpe-v3.
Mei: quick experiments to run (small matrix):
  1) run merged-int4 but force customer's tokenizer at decode time (--tokenizer=/mnt/cust/zenobia/tokenizer_v1.json)
  2) remap LoRA deltas to our tokenizer before merge using `remap-lora-tokens` then rebuild merged weights
  3) ablation: int4 default vs int4+per-channel-clip vs int8 vs fp32
Noor: queued jobs: job-A (int4+cust-tokenizer), job-B (remap+merge+int4), job-C (int4+clip). infra reports they'll run on ml-qa-2, ETA ~25m.
QA-bot: added `--detok-preserve-numeric` flag to all runs for debug output.
Carlos: if remap eliminates majority of errors, that's our preferred short-term fix. remap is cheap and keeps int4 perf. If not, fallback to int8 for the customer's route until we can craft a robust per-customer quant profile.
Mei: note: also check LoRA training logs for any pre-tokenization normalization (e.g., stripping commas). if LoRA was trained on pre-normalized text, it may not have learned tokens for commas at all, causing missing separators after merge.
Noor: good catch. I inspected their training manifest: they applied "normalize_numbers: true" and also used a custom preprocessor that removed commas from numbers. So their LoRA deltas expect numerics without commas.
Carlos: that explains the "12300" result. The merged model decodes according to base tokenizer which expects commas; but LoRA never corrected for comma tokens, so output can be inconsistent. Two remediation paths: a) remap+remerge with token mapping that preserves numeric tokens (preferred), b) re-encode LoRA into our token space by replaying deltas on re-tokenized embeddings (heavier), c) shipping a decode-time shim that inserts commas (hacky).
Mei: run results just in: job-A (int4 + cust-tokenizer at decode) improved EM_format from 0.68 -> 0.89 (n=400). job-B (remap+merge+int4) improved EM_format -> 0.97; MAE dropped to 0.08. job-C (int4 + per-channel clip threshold=3.0) gave EM 0.92, MAE 0.19.
Noor: remap+merge clearly best. I'll keep int4 with remapped LoRA as the rollout candidate.
Carlos: operational checklist before rollout: 1) add a canary route for customer tagged to remapped-int4 model for 1000 requests, 2) enable fallback to merged-int8 if EM_format drops >3% in first hour, 3) add alert on TokenSplitRate for numerics >0.02.
Mei: also add a gating test to LoRA onboarding CI: synthetic numeric pack with thousands, decimals, negative, parentheses; require token-id overlap for punctuation/numeric tokens >= 99.9% or automatic remap step. I'll open a tiny PR to add this to onboarding pipeline.
CS: please draft a short note to customer explaining: reason (tokenization+quant sensitivity), mitigation (remap+remerge into int4, canary and fallback to int8), ETA (~2 hours for canary + monitoring). I'll approve message.
Noor: drafted note and PR for prod-config canary; pushing artifacts to /artifacts/zenobia/merge-17432.
QA-bot: canary job created: route=customer/zenobia/model=zenobia-remap-int4, sample-size=1000, fallback=zenobia-int8, monitor metrics: EM_format, TokenSplitRate, MAE_amounts.
Noor: canary started. initial 100 samples: EM_format=0.98, TokenSplitRate=0.004, MAE=0.09. looks good.
Carlos: nice job. follow-ups: 1) commit remap tooling improvements to handle common numeric normalization patterns automatically, 2) KB entry for CS + playbook for rapid customer rollback, 3) add numeric synthetic pack to standard evalpacks.
Mei: filing tasks now. closing thread once KB and prod-config are merged. :white_check_mark:
